latest.title: OPERATIONAL UPDATE: 10KG GOLD PRODUCED IN AUGUST
latest.content:
7 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 5650T
Amigo Resources PLC
07 September 2026
NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OF SUCH JURISDICTION.
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
7 September 2026
Amigo Resources PLC
("Amigo" or the "Company")
OPERATIONAL UPDATE: 10KG GOLD PRODUCED IN AUGUST
Amigo Resources PLC
(LSE: AMGO) is pleased to present an operational update on its gold production activities in Tanzania.
Highlights
·
August Production Milestone:
Achieved total gold production of 10 kilograms during August 2026.
·
100% Gravity-Based Recovery:
All gold recovered to date has been produced entirely through physical gravity concentration (free gold), without chemical reagents or leaching.
·
Initial Gravity Circuit Commissioned:
Primary gravity circuits at Mojimoto and Kabete are fully operational. A temporary startup bottleneck was resolved, with routine optimisation ongoing.
·
Structured Monthly Reporting:
Following gravity circuit stabilisation, Amigo targets the formalisation and resumption of its regular monthly operational reporting (covering production, physical sales, and realised revenue) starting in October 2026.
·
Stockpiling for Secondary Processing:
Gravity tailings are being systematically stockpiled on-site for secondary chemical leaching to maximise total metallurgical recovery.
·
Leaching Circuit Mobilisation:
Fabrication and procurement of chemical leaching equipment - including heavy-duty slurry tanks and high-capacity pumps - are underway, with site installation and commissioning targeted for early Q4 2026.
·
Plant Expansion On Schedule:
High-capacity grinding and crushing equipment is in transit to Tanzania, with commissioning of the expanded plant remaining on track for early Q4 2026.
Gold Production and Plant Development
During August 2026, Amigo's Tanzanian operations at Mojimoto and Kabete produced 10 kilograms of gold following the successful commissioning of the primary gravity circuit.
Gold recovered to date has been produced exclusively through physical gravity concentration, utilising water and mineral density differentials to isolate free gold without chemical reagents. Residual process materials and tailings are being systematically stockpiled on-site. This strategy enables early cash flow generation through free gold extraction while preserving high-grade tailings for secondary treatment.
The upcoming chemical leaching phase will incorporate heavy-duty slurry tanks, high-capacity pumps, and automated Carbon-in-Leach (CIL) circuits. Construction of this secondary circuit is progressing on schedule for targeted commissioning in early Q4 2026. Subject to final metallurgical confirmation and operational commissioning, processing stockpiled tailings through the leaching circuit is expected to significantly increase total gold recovery rates.
An operational bottleneck encountered within the gravity circuit during initial August startup has been fully resolved. Routine technical optimisation continues as the Company scales plant throughput, while continuously addressing local grid power stability and equipment reliability.
Following the stabilisation of the initial gravity circuit and the transition to larger-scale operations, Amigo targets initiating regular monthly operational reporting on gold production, sales, and revenue starting in October 2026. Future throughput rates and recovery milestones remain conditional on the timely installation of the expanded plant, ore feed characteristics, and ongoing metallurgical performance.
Next Phase of Plant Development
Following proven free gold recovery through primary gravity circuits, Amigo's immediate operational priority is expanding processing capacity across Mojimoto and Kabete through two key objectives:
·
Capacity Expansion:
Installing larger gravity-separation machinery to increase run-of-mine ore throughput and maximise free gold capture.
·
Secondary Recovery Circuit:
Completing the chemical leaching circuit to optimise total metallurgical recovery per tonne of ore processed.
Procurement for the expanded processing plant was previously completed by the Company's Tanzanian subsidiaries. Equipment is currently in transit to site, with delivery, installation, and commissioning expected in early Q4 2026.
Craig Ransley, Executive Chair of Amigo Resources PLC, commented:
"Achieving 10 kilograms of gold production strictly through gravity recovery represents critical operational validation of Amigo's processing model in Tanzania. While we encountered a minor processing bottleneck during the initial August startup, our site team resolved the issue swiftly and effectively.
With gravity-only recovery proven, our immediate focus turns toward completing the installation and commissioning of the expanded plant in early Q4 2026. This next phase will allow us to process stockpiled tailings through integrated secondary circuits, optimising total metallurgical recovery per tonne and driving long-term value across our Tanzanian assets.
Having established a stable operational foundation, Amigo looks forward to commencing its formal monthly reporting cycle on gold production, sales, and revenue starting in October 2026."

latest.title: Letter to Update Shareholders from Craig Ransley
latest.content:
24 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 7590R
Amigo Resources PLC
24 August 2026
NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OF SUCH JURISDICTION.
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
24 August 2026
Amigo Resources PLC
("Amigo" or the "Company")
Letter to Update Shareholders from Craig Ransley, Executive Chair
- Adoption of Dividend Policy
G'day All!
Following my previous update to you on 31 July 2026, where I detailed our transition into an active, production-ready mining house, I am writing today to announce another key milestone.
As promised in my last letter, we are focused on transforming Amigo into a free cash flow generative gold producer in the shortest possible term.
The Board has formally adopted our first dividend policy.
Our target under this new policy is clear:
to deliver our inaugural dividend within the next 12 months
.
We have established a robust policy framework to support this, which is appended to this announcement. We set out with a clear mandate to build a company that prioritises the interests of its actual owners. This policy adoption aligns directly with making Amigo a premier, dividend-producing mining company.
I look forward to the exciting times ahead as we scale our gold processing operations. Our team will keep you updated, and I look forward to letting you know the moment we are in a position to distribute our first dividend.
As I have stressed before, our leadership team are operators focused on real results on the ground. We are shareholders ourselves, meaning our interests are fully aligned with yours. We are here to mine the resource in the ground rather than mining the share market.
To support this policy while avoiding equity dilution, we remain committed to a disciplined funding strategy, keeping capital-raising requirements at the project subsidiary level. This ensures that as Tanzanian operations scale up, the resulting cash flows are directed into the vault and ultimately back to you as dividends.
Thank you for your continued support as we put gold in the vault and build a world-class, yield-producing platform.
Adios Amigos!
Yours sincerely,
Craig Ransley
Executive Chair
Amigo Resources PLC

Dividend Policy
1 Overview
This Dividend Policy (Policy) sets out the position of Amigo Resources PLC (the Company) in relation to the declaration and payment of dividends from distributable profits, in accordance with the Companies Act 2006. This Policy provides general guidance only and does not constitute a commitment to pay dividends.
2 Declaration and Payment of Dividends
(a) The declaration and payment of dividends is at the discretion of the Board of Directors of the Company (the Directors):
(i) Interim dividends may be declared by the Directors at any time.
(ii) Final dividends may only be paid following shareholder approval at a general meeting.
(b) The Policy of the Company is to distribute to shareholders a portion of distributable profits, subject to the Directors assessment of:
(i) the recognition of profit and availability of cash for distribution;
(ii) any banking or other funding requirements by which the Company is bound from time to time;
(iii) the operating and investment needs of the Company;
(iv) working capital requirements for the Company and its subsidiaries;
(v) the anticipated future growth and earnings of the Company;
(vi) provisions of the Company's Articles of Association; and
(vii) any relevant applicable laws.
(c) The Policy of the Company in relation to dividends is as follows:
(i) The Company proposes, but does not commit, to consider paying dividends on a semi-annual basis:
(ii) The Directors will endeavour, where appropriate, to maintain a dividend payout ratio of between 40% and 80% of net profit after tax attributable to the Company, subject to the considerations outlined above.
(iii) The Board retains full discretion to vary or suspend dividends at any time.
(iv) All dividends will comply with the London Stock Exchange Dividend Procedure Timetable.
(d) The Directors shall be responsible for all resolutions on the declaration and payment of dividends and will formally record such decisions in Directors minutes, including confirmation of available distributable profits.
(e) The Board of Directors provide no guarantee as to:
(i) the extent of future dividends; and
(ii) the tax treatment of such dividends.
(f) The Company will not declare any dividend where prohibited by law, including where the Company does not have sufficient distributable profits or where the Directors have reasonable grounds to believe that the Company would, after payment, be unable to meet its liabilities as they fall due.
(g) The list of persons entitled to receive dividends at the record date shall be prepared by the Company's Share Registrar in accordance with the Company's instructions and applicable legislation. Dividend announcements will include the required LSE fields, including:
(i) gross dividend amount and currency;
(ii) type of dividend (interim/final);
(iii) record date;
(iv) payment date;
(v) ISIN(s) and TIDM; and
(vi) details of any scrip, DRIP, or currency election options.
(h) The Company must comply with the provisions of its Articles of Association, the Companies Act 2006, the UK Listing Rules, the Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules (DTRs), and the London Stock Exchange Admission and Disclosure Standards in relation to the declaration and payment of dividends.
Disclaimer
The Policy provides general guidance only and does not constitute a commitment or forecast regarding future dividends. Dividend decisions remain entirely at the discretion of the Directors.
Amendment
This Policy shall be effective from the date of execution and may be amended, replaced or revoked at any time by the Directors.
The Directors to review this Policy on an annual basis.

latest.content:

Amigo Resources PLC

NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OF SUCH JURISDICTION.
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 21 August 2026
Amigo Resources PLC
("Amigo" or the "Company")
Memorandum of Understanding with the State Mining Corporation of Tanzania
Amigo Resources PLC
(LSE: AMGO), the Africa-focused gold and critical minerals company, is pleased to announce that it has entered into a Memorandum of Understanding ("
MOU
") with the State Mining Corporation of Tanzania (the Tanzanian state enterprise mandated to co-develop, manage, and commercialise key mineral resources across Tanzania) ("
STAMICO
"). The MOU establishes a strategic collaboration framework to evaluate a significant graphite tailings recovery and beneficiation project within the project areas in Tanzania (the "
Project
").
Highlights
·
High-Value Strategic Collaboration:
Establishment of a collaborative framework for technical, commercial, and regulatory assessment, aiming to transform historical graphite-bearing material into a saleable mineral product.
·
Resource Efficiency & Circular Mining:
Evaluation of graphite-bearing tailings, dumps, and stockpiles to optimise resource efficiency and promote value-addition within Tanzania.
·
Exclusivity:
STAMICO has granted Amigo exclusivity regarding third-party discussions for the term of the MOU, providing the parties time to negotiate definitive long-form agreements.
·
Amigo to Lead Operations:
Amigo will direct and finance a comprehensive technical due diligence programme, including sampling, metallurgical testing, and independent laboratory analysis.
·
National Stakeholder Engagement:
STAMICO will coordinate engagement with relevant Tanzanian Government institutions and local artisanal mining communities to ensure inclusive participation.
Project Rationale
The Project is centred on the productive reuse of graphite-bearing material that is currently regarded as having limited value. Subject to satisfactory due diligence, the Project aims to deliver superior resource efficiency, support the environmental management of historical residues, and create an additional source of income for eligible local miners and material owners.
Principal Terms of the MOU
The MOU records the parties' present intentions to determine the feasibility of the Project and establishes a pathway toward binding long-form contracts:
·
Responsibilities:
Amigo is responsible for directing technical due diligence. STAMICO will coordinate engagement with relevant authorities and facilitate physical access to the Project area and non-confidential technical data.
·
Intellectual Property:
Amigo retains sole and exclusive ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property, including proprietary methodologies.
·
Legal Status:
While the broader MOU is non-binding regarding the ultimate development of the Project, specific provisions relating to exclusivity, confidentiality, costs, term, governing law, and dispute resolution are legally binding.
Next Steps & Definitive Agreements
The assessment period provides STAMICO and Amigo time to negotiate definitive long-form agreements. Amigo intends to begin a structured due-diligence programme comprising representative sampling, mineralogical testing, and preliminary technical and commercial evaluation. If results are satisfactory, the parties intend to negotiate exclusively and in good faith toward a definitive agreement for the development of the Project.
Craig Ransley, Executive Chair of Amigo Resources PLC, commented:
"This MOU gives Amigo and STAMICO the opportunity to determine whether graphite-bearing material that is currently unused or regarded as waste can be transformed into a valuable mineral product. The potential significance of the Project extends beyond graphite recovery; if successful, it could improve the productive use and management of historical mining residues while creating an additional income opportunity for eligible local miners and material owners.
Our approach combines resource efficiency, local participation and Tanzanian value addition. We will now focus on verifying the quantity, grade, mineralogy and metallurgical characteristics of the available material before determining whether the Project can progress to a definitive development agreement.
"
Dr. Venance Mwasse, Managing Director of STAMICO commented:
"STAMICO welcomes this cooperation with Amigo Resources PLC to evaluate the recovery and beneficiation of graphite from historical tailings, dumps and stockpiles within the Project area. This initiative has the potential to support Tanzania's objectives of mineral beneficiation, environmental responsibility and inclusive participation in the mining sector. Recovering value from currently unused material could improve resource efficiency while creating additional economic opportunities for miners and surrounding communities. STAMICO will work with Amigo and local stakeholders to ensure the opportunity is assessed transparently and in accordance with Tanzanian law. This is a good beginning, and we should treat it as a stepping stone towards a wider scope of collaboration, given the many opportunities available."
About the State Mining Corporation of Tanzania (STAMICO)
The State Mining Corporation of Tanzania (STAMICO) is a Tanzania state-owned entity established under the Public Corporations Act of Tanzania. STAMICO is tasked with participating in, and advancing commercial development across Tanzania's mining sector. It is the primary government vehicle for partnership with strategic investors in the mining sector, and its mandate is to invest in the entire mineral value chain from exploration, mining, value addition and trading.

latest.content:

NOT FOR RELEASE, PUBLICATION OR DISTRIBUTION, IN WHOLE OR IN PART, IN, INTO OR FROM ANY JURISDICTION WHERE TO DO SO WOULD CONSTITUTE A VIOLATION OF THE RELEVANT LAWS OF SUCH JURISDICTION.
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 3 August 2026
Amigo Resources PLC
("Amigo" or the "Company")
Production Update: Achievement of First 5kg Gold Milestone
Amigo Resources PLC (LSE: AMGO) is pleased to announce that its Tanzanian processing operations have produced 5 kilograms of gold since the commissioning of processing activities. This achievement marks the Company's first meaningful production and serves as a formal validation of the Group's vertically integrated mining and processing strategy.
Highlights
·
Significant Production Milestone:
Achievement of the first 5 kilograms of gold produced between the start of commissioning (as announced on 24 July 2026) and 31 July 2026 from the Company's Mojimoto and Kabete operations.
·
Operational Validation:
Successful transition from infrastructure commissioning into active production levels, validating the Group's organically developed Tanzanian hubs.
·
Optimisation Underway:
Throughput and recovery optimisation is currently in progress, with production levels expected to increase over the coming weeks.
·
Inaugural Report:
This announcement constitutes the Company's first monthly production update under the new transparency standard established to provide regular data to the market.
Operational Achievement: 5kg Milestone
The achievement of the first 5 kilograms of gold represents the definitive transition from vision to execution for Amigo's Tanzanian assets and is a validation of its development model. Both processing plants are now operating successfully, establishing the necessary foundation for a planned ramp-up in throughput and recoveries. Current activity remains focused on technical optimisation as processing rates are progressively increased.
Craig Ransley, Executive Chair of Amigo Resources PLC, commented:
"Producing our first 5kg of gold is a landmark milestone that validates Amigo's evolution from vision to execution. Following our announcement on 24 July 2026 that processing had been commissioned, we have established successful operations at Mojimoto and Kabete in short order, delivering these figures as at 31 July 2026.
This specific achievement represents our first meaningful commercial recovery and serves as a formal proof of concept for our vertically integrated mining model.
While these early figures represent the first stage of our journey, they provide a robust platform for the rapid scale-up we have planned. Our team is now focused on throughput and recovery optimisation across both plants, with production levels expected to increase steadily over the coming weeks.
Our transition to a standardised monthly reporting cycle begins with this inaugural July report, reflecting our commitment to the transparency required to value Amigo as an established producer. We remain focused on ramping up our Tanzanian hubs safely and efficiently as we continue to deliver gold to the vault".

Amigo is focussed on gold and rare earth mining opportunities in Africa, principally in Tanzania and Mauritania. The Amigo Shares are listed on the Official List of the Financial Conduct Authority and traded on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange

company_30s.what_they_do: Amigo Gold Limited is a small‑cap gold mining company focused on exploration and early production in Tanzania. Its main asset is the Musensi Hill project, where it has begun producing gold on a very modest scale.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Gold remains a safe‑haven commodity, and a low‑cost, high‑grade producer can quickly become valuable if prices climb. The Musensi Hill project also contains rare‑earth elements, adding a diversification angle that could attract investors looking for niche assets.
company_30s.current_state: The firm has moved from exploration into first‑time production, delivering 10 kg of gold in August and 5 kg earlier in the year. Cash burn is still a concern, but the company is beginning to generate revenue from gold sales. The share price is trading near the bottom of its 52‑week range, reflecting the steep decline seen in recent months.

rns_narrative: The company’s announcements focus on incremental gold production and the progression of the Musensi Hill project. The latest update confirms a 10 kg gold output for August, a milestone that signals operational momentum.

A second theme is corporate restructuring and shareholder communication: management changes, a new memorandum of understanding, and updates to the accounting reference date all point to an effort to streamline operations and improve transparency.
Together, these events suggest the firm is stabilizing its cash flow and preparing to scale its Tanzanian operations.

near_term_catalysts: Q3 earnings release – if the company can show a positive cash flow or a new gold sale contract, it could spark a bounce.
Announcement of a new mining lease or a cost‑reduction agreement in Tanzania, which would improve margins.
A significant rise in global gold prices (e.g., above $2,100/oz) that would lift the intrinsic value of the company’s production.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that exceeds 150% of the 20‑day average and a break of the 10‑week low. A clear technical support at the 52‑week low would also reinforce a mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The share appears to be in the early stages of a potential recovery – it has already fallen deep but has not yet entered a sustained washout. A small catalyst, such as a positive earnings report, could trigger a rebound if the market believes the company can sustain production.

buy_vs_sell.lean: Neutral – there is no clear signal color or confirmed deep crash data, but the dead trends and low engagement give a contrarian edge.
buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company can prove it will keep producing and the gold price rises, the share could recover to the midpoint of its 52‑week range, delivering roughly a 50% upside from the current level. The asymmetry is favorable because the downside is capped by the low price floor, while upside potential is amplified by the gold price lift.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risk is that the firm will not be able to sustain production or reduce costs, leading to another slide. A failure to secure new leases or contracts could push the share back below its 52‑week low.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the current low price; potential gain could be 2‑3× that loss if the share climbs to the midpoint. The ratio is roughly 1:2.5 to 1:3, making it an attractive asymmetrical play if the catalyst materializes.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price closes above the 10‑week low with volume 20% higher than the 20‑day average. Size the position so that a 5% drop would trigger a stop, keeping risk below 1–2% of the trading account.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until a clear sign of operational improvement – e.g., a new lease, a cost‑reduction agreement, or a gold price spike – before committing. Watch for a 20‑day moving‑average crossover as a confirmation.
playbook.if_passing: No imminent terminal risk has been identified, so the ‘passing’ scenario is not applicable.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Amigo Gold is a very small, early‑production miner that has just hit a production milestone; with no public interest and a potential catalyst in Q3 earnings, it presents a contrarian, asymmetrical upside if the market believes it can sustain operations.
